data.title: Network Traffic Manipulation
data.summary: The sample intercepts and alters network traffic in transit — injecting content into unencrypted responses, redirecting requests, or modifying DNS resolution — rather than merely observing it.
data.description:
This requires a position in the traffic path, achieved either through a host-level
capability (a local proxy, a modified hosts file or resolver, a malicious browser
extension) or a network-level one (ARP spoofing, a compromised router). The result is
content the victim did not request and did not come from the legitimate server — injected
advertising, a swapped download link, or a redirected login page — delivered over a
connection that otherwise looks normal.
data.recommendation:
* Identify the interception point (local proxy configuration, hosts file, DNS settings, network device) rather than only the manipulated content observed.
* Compare traffic at the suspected interception point against a known-clean capture of the same destination to confirm manipulation versus legitimate server-side content.
* Where the interception is network-level rather than host-level, scope the investigation to every host on the affected network segment, not only the one where symptoms were observed.
data.short_recommendation: Identify the interception point itself (proxy, DNS, network device), not only the manipulated content observed.

mitre_techniques.procedure: Installed a local proxy configuration that injected advertising content into unencrypted HTTP responses in transit.

mbc_techniques.implementation: Local proxy rewrote unencrypted HTTP response bodies in transit to inject additional content.
